I'm not that knowledgeable about what directx does, but doesn't opengl do the same thing?

Yes and no. DirectX is responsible for several things related to graphics, sound, peripherals and system resource management - among the many things it can do is a unified library for graphics called Direct3D. OpenGL is graphics only, so when you're comparing DirectX to OpenGL, it's more appropriate to compare Direct3D (or DirectDraw if you're talking pre-DX8 2D rendering) to OpenGL.

DirectX has a lot of advantages for talking to many different kinds of hardware in a common way. Since it's proprietary, the only target you're trying to hit as a programmer is a specific version of DirectX rather than a series of differing implementations. OpenGL on the other hand has a rather long and sorted history with its implementations which lead to some fragmentation. Traditionally the method used to deal with this fragmentation was to write (or use) a specific opengl driver implementation that you can bundle with your application. It's much better than it used to be, but is still only one piece of the puzzle when you're talking game development.

The arguments surrounding DirectX and OpenGL are multi-faceted and often quite technical, but it's safe to say that a "which is better" argument is never as black and white as we'd like it to be. Both have their pros and cons. There's also a long history of events that lead up to Direct3D being generally preferred by most devs over OpenGL.

If you're interested in learning a bit more about this and don't mind a history lesson to assist your understanding, this post contains a fascinating comment made by a professional OpenGL dev that is very detailed and well written.
